metadata.title: Wan 3.0 — Turn Documents and Pages Into Video | Oddbeam
metadata.description: Wan 3.0 on Oddbeam is Alibaba's omni-reference model: feed it a product page, a PDF, or a deck alongside your prompt, and get up to 30 seconds of 1080P with native audio. 40 credits per clip — 20 on Unlimited.

hero.title: Wan 3.0 Video Generator
hero.description: The brief itself becomes the input. Alibaba's Wan 3.0 takes a webpage, a PDF, or a slide deck as reference material next to your prompt — and renders up to 30 seconds of continuous 1080P with native audio in one pass. Up to 20 reference assets per job, at 40 credits the lowest per-clip rate among 30-second models.

usage.title: From Source Material to Screen
usage.description: Wan 3.0 starts from what your business already has — the workflow:

items.title: Attach the Source, Not Just a Prompt
items.description: Point it at a product page or hand it a PDF, DOCX, or slide deck — Wan 3.0 parses the document and uses its content as scene material for the video.

items.title: Stack Your References
items.description: Mix up to 10 images, 5 video clips, and 5 audio files in one job — a character image, a camera-move reference, and a mood track all wire into the same generation.

items.title: Plan the Full 30 Seconds
items.description: Write the shot as one continuous take — setup, action, transition, payoff. Wan 3.0's native 30-second window is built for complete stories, not stitched fragments.

items.title: Draft Cheap, Finish Clean
items.description: Iterate at 480P where per-second cost is a fraction of 1080P, then re-render the keeper at 720P or full 1080P with audio on — same prompt, graded output.

features.title: What 'Omni-Reference' Actually Buys
features.description: The capabilities that make Wan 3.0 the source-material model on Oddbeam:

items.title: Documents and webpages become footage
items.description: Feed one document — PDF, DOCX, PPTX, Markdown — or one public webpage per job, and Wan 3.0 parses it into scene material. A product page turns into a launch film; a courseware file into an explainer.

items.title: 30 seconds in one continuous take
items.description: Twice the previous generation's ceiling: a single pass holds a setup, ordered action, a transition, and a payoff — complete stories that shorter models force you to stitch.

items.title: Up to 20 reference assets
items.description: Combine as many as 10 images, 5 video clips, and 5 audio files per job — identity, motion, and mood each get their own pinned source, referenced positionally in the prompt.

items.title: Consistency for production workflows
items.description: Faces, wardrobe, product geometry, logos, and scene relationships hold across the take — the pixel-level consistency that makes client delivery predictable instead of a re-roll lottery.

items.title: The lowest rate per 30-second story
items.description: 40 credits per clip — 20 on Unlimited, 16 yearly — with audio on or off per generation. Among 30-second-class models, Wan 3.0 is the one you can afford to explore with.

testimonials.title: Built on Existing Material
testimonials.description: Teams that start from documents, not blank prompts.

items.name: Product Marketing Manager
items.quote: I paste the product page URL and brief the shot — the launch video comes back matching the copy that's already live. No screenshot collages, no retyping specs.

items.name: Corporate L&D Producer
items.quote: Slide decks in, narrated explainers out — Wan 3.0 reads the PDF and stages it. Thirty seconds of 1080P at 40 credits made our courseware backlog shippable.

items.name: Short Drama Showrunner
items.quote: A 30-second continuous take with faces and wardrobe that hold — that's an entire scene unit per render, at the cheapest rate on our whole model roster.

items.question: How much does Wan 3.0 cost per video?
items.answer: Wan 3.0 costs 40 credits per generation on Oddbeam for Starter and Pro plans — the lowest rate among 30-second-class models. Unlimited plan subscribers pay 20 credits per clip, and yearly Unlimited brings it to 16. The Starter plan's 2,500 monthly credits cover about 62 clips.

items.question: Can Wan 3.0 use documents or webpages as input?
items.answer: Yes — it accepts one document per job (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, Markdown and more, up to 100MB and 50 pages) or one public webpage link, parses the content, and uses it as scene material alongside your prompt. A product page or slide deck becomes source footage.

items.question: How long can a Wan 3.0 video be?
items.answer: Up to 30 seconds in one continuous native generation — double the previous Wan generation's ceiling — with first/last frame control available for anchoring a shot's entry and exit.

items.question: How many references can Wan 3.0 take?
items.answer: Up to 20 reference assets per job: as many as 10 images, 5 video clips, and 5 audio clips. Reference them positionally in the prompt — Image 1, Video 2 — and each contributes identity, motion, or mood to the same generation.

items.question: What resolutions does Wan 3.0 support?
items.answer: 480P, 720P, and 1080P across five aspect ratios from 16:9 to 9:16, with native audio generated in the same pass or toggled off for silent masters. Draft at 480P, deliver at 1080P.

items.question: Wan 3.0 or MiniMax H3 — which should I pick?
items.answer: Pick Wan 3.0 for source-driven storytelling: documents and webpages as input, 30-second takes, 20 reference slots, at 40 credits. Pick MiniMax H3 for audio-led performance and 2K output at 100 credits. Wan turns material into video; H3 conducts media into performance.
